subject: Pilot ops & evaluation choreography — Vertex Health
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ops & evaluation choreography — Vertex Health

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning — productive session and great visibility into the clinical workflow you want to augment. Below is a concise recap and a proposed lightweight pilot / evaluation choreography so we can lock owners and timelines. Please confirm or suggest changes.

Recap (brief):
- Goal: Reduce triage time for intake nurses by surfacing suggested clinical coding and next-step phrasing for common admission notes.
- Constraint: PHI must not leave Vertex-managed VPC during the pilot; logging must be redacted.
- Traffic shape: ~5k daily note submissions across 3 clinics; target pilot samples ~2-3% of traffic for shadowing.

Proposed success criteria (suggested, please validate):
1) Accuracy (clinically actionable suggestions accepted by clinicians) >= 65% on sampled cases.
2) Hallucination rate (clinically unsafe suggestions) < 2% on evaluated set.
3) 95th percentile response latency < 600ms for accepted traffic.
4) Token cost per request within agreed SOW budget (TBD).

Evaluation plan (two-stage, low-risk):
A) Offline eval (pre-deploy) — Redwood runs an offline grading of 300 canonical prompts + 200 anonymized Vertex examples you provide. Grading rubric will include: clinical correctness, hallucination flag, instruction-following, and token cost estimate.
B) Shadow pilot (live, non-blocking) — 2-week shadow against sampled live traffic (2–3% sample). Results feed into final acceptance.

Ownership / next steps:
- Vertex: provide anonymized sample set (200 examples) and security contact for data handling sign-off.
- Redwood: deliver offline eval report and scoring rubric; run shadow pilot and provide aggregated metrics and example failure cases.
- Proposed owners: Rishi (commercial, overall), Marissa (technical lead/CS), Aditya (integration lead).

Timeline (tentative):
- Kickoff & data handoff: week of 6/29
- Offline eval delivery: by 7/13
- Shadow pilot: 7/14–7/28
- Acceptance review: by 7/31

Attachments: draft rubric + data handling checklist included (vertex_eval_rubric_v1.xlsx; data_handling_matrix.pdf).

If that looks good, I’ll prepare an SOW stub and DocuSign for signatures and loop in our security contact to align on redaction/KMS.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

> Recap (brief):
> - Goal: Reduce triage time for intake nurses by surfacing suggested clinical coding and next-step phrasing for common admission notes.
> - Constraint: PHI must not leave Vertex-managed VPC during the pilot; logging must be redacted.

All correct. To confirm: we can provide anonymized examples but will need to understand exactly what fields Redwood needs to run the offline eval (free-text notes? diagnosis codes?). Our security team (security@vertexhealth.com) should be looped in for the VPC/shadow specifics.

About success criteria: the 65% acceptance rate is reasonable as a starting point. Can you clarify how you define "clinically actionable" versus simple format suggestions? Also would prefer hallucination < 1.5% if possible.

For the shadow pilot: we can do 2% sampling but only if requests are redacted before leaving our network — is Redwood able to run the shadow inside our VPC (private deployment) or will traffic be proxied? We want to avoid exporting identifiable PHI.

Please include Tom Lee (Clinical Ops) on the follow-ups (tom.lee@vertexhealth.com).

Thanks —
Sarah
Product Lead, Clinical Informatics
Vertex Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@vertexhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ops & evaluation choreography — Vertex Health

Thanks — picking this up from a tech/ops perspective. Short answers first, then details.

1) Offline eval dataset requirements:
- Preferred: de-identified free-text notes + ground-truth clinician action (accepted suggestion / corrected suggestion). If ground-truth not available, we can use clinician-annotated labels (1/0 + reason).
- Minimum: 200 de-identified examples with a short context field (encounter type + note snippet).

2) Grading rubric (proposed axes):
- Clinical correctness (binary + short rationale)
- Safety/hallucination flag (binary)
- Relevance / specificity (3-level scale: low/med/high)
- Latency bucket (p50/p95)
- Token cost estimate (avg tokens per request)

Acceptance thresholds (proposal):
- Clinical correctness >= 65%
- Safety/hallucination < 1.5% (per Sarah’s ask)
- p95 latency < 600ms for requests routed to Redwood Dedicated or Private setup

3) Shadow mode options and data handling:
- Option A (preferred for Vertex): Redwood Private deployment inside Vertex VPC (we provide AMI/container) — no PHI leaves VPC; Redwood provides support and remote instrumentation.
- Option B: Proxy + strong client-side redaction (Vertex redacts PHI before sending); Redwood receives redacted payloads in hosted environment.

Instrumentation & logs:
- We’ll produce an aggregated metrics dashboard (no raw PHI): acceptance rate by prompt bucket, confusion examples, top hallucination triggers.
- For fail cases we’ll request minimal context + redacted text for debugging.

Attachments: I’m attaching the evaluation rubric (vertex_eval_rubric_v1.xlsx) and a short data-handling matrix (data_handling_matrix.pdf) with the options above.

Let me know if we should tighten any thresholds; otherwise I’ll bake this into the pilot SOW and schedule a technical kickoff with Vertex infra.

—
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
